subject: psychiatry
title: Dissociative and Functional Neurological Symptom Disorders

steps.tx: **Dissociative amnesia** involves an inability to recall important personal autobiographical information, usually of a traumatic or stressful nature, that is inconsistent with ordinary forgetfulness. Memory loss is typically localized to a specific traumatic event or selective for certain aspects, while procedural and semantic memory remains intact.
steps.say: Dissociative amnesia is the inability to recall personal autobiographical trauma, far exceeding ordinary forgetfulness while procedural memory remains preserved.

left.title: Dissociative Amnesia
points: Procedural memory and general intellect intact

right.title: Organic Cerebral Amnesia
points: Ribot law: older memories preserved over recent

steps.tx: **Dissociative fugue** is a specialized specifier of dissociative amnesia characterized by sudden, unexpected, purposeful travel away from home or customary workplace, accompanied by amnesia for one's identity. Patients may assume a completely new identity and occupation during the fugue state, waking with total amnesia for the journey.
steps.say: Dissociative fugue involves sudden purposeful travel away from home with loss of identity, sometimes assuming a new persona before spontaneous recovery.

nodes.label: Severe psychological crisis, financial disaster, or military trauma
Sudden purposeful travel away from home with identity amnesia
Establishment of new social identity or transient vagrancy
Abrupt return of original identity with amnesia for fugue period

steps.tx: **Dissociative identity disorder**, formerly multiple personality disorder, is characterized by the presence of two or more distinct personality states or alters that recurrently take control of the individual's behavior. Each identity exhibits distinct names, mannerisms, voices, and memories, linked etiologically to severe, chronic childhood abuse.
steps.say: Dissociative identity disorder features two or more distinct personality states alternating executive control, strongly linked to severe childhood trauma.

left.title: Diagnostic Features
points: Two or more distinct personality states (alters)
Recurrent gaps in everyday autobiographical memory
Severe childhood physical or sexual trauma history
Not caused by substance intoxication or seizures

right.title: Psychotherapeutic Goals
points: Integration of alters into a unified identity

steps.tx: Watch the examiner's hands in this picture as the patient pushes the good leg down against resistance. In **Hoover sign**, the supposedly weak leg presses down involuntarily at the same moment, revealing that its extensor pathway works when attention is directed elsewhere. A positive sign supports functional weakness, although it should be shared with the patient as evidence of reversibility, not as an accusation.
steps.say: When the strong leg flexes against resistance, the weak leg extends on its own in Hoover sign. That reveals intact power and supports functional weakness.

vis.alt: Clinical Hoover sign examination for functional leg weakness, with involuntary extension of the weak leg during contralateral hip flexion
vis.caption: Clinical Hoover sign test for functional lower extremity weakness, demonstrating involuntary contralateral hip extension. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Conversion disorder**, designated functional neurological symptom disorder, presents with one or more symptoms of altered voluntary motor or sensory function that are clinically incompatible with recognized neurological or medical conditions. Common manifestations include psychogenic non-epileptic seizures, functional paraplegia, aphonia, blindness, and sensory anaesthesia.
steps.say: Conversion disorder involves motor or sensory deficits incompatible with neurological pathology, such as functional paralysis or non-epileptic seizures.

vis.title: Conversion Presentations & Signs
rows: Avoidance of obstacles; normal visual evoked potentials
Intact vocal cord adduction during coughing
Cough produces loud sound; unable to whisper words
Cutaneous nerves overlap across midline anatomically

steps.tx: **La belle indifference** is an historical clinical sign classically associated with conversion disorder, wherein the patient displays an incongruous, serene lack of concern or anxiety regarding their severe physical disability, such as sudden paraplegia. However, modern diagnostic criteria do not rely on it due to low specificity.
steps.say: La belle indifference describes an unusual lack of emotional distress despite sudden physical paralysis, though modern criteria do not require it.

left.title: Historical Concept
points: Attributed to primary gain reducing conflict

right.title: Modern Clinical Reality
points: Present in under thirty percent of conversion cases
Also seen in severe organic illnesses (anosognosia)

steps.tx: When episodes look like convulsions, recording brain waves during one settles the argument. Epileptic seizures march with rhythmic epileptiform discharges that build and spread across the tracing as limbs jerk in time. Functional episodes thrash, roll and thrust while the background rhythm stays awake and orderly throughout. Capturing a typical event on **video-EEG monitoring** is therefore the reference test whenever the history cannot separate the two.
steps.say: Video EEG records a typical episode, showing epileptiform discharges in epilepsy and a normal awake background in functional attacks.

vis.alt: Split video EEG display comparing rhythmic epileptiform discharges during an epileptic seizure with a normal awake tracing during a psychogenic non-epileptic episode
vis.caption: Rhythmic epileptiform discharges accompanying an epileptic convulsion on one side, with an orderly awake tracing during a psychogenic episode on the other. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Pseudoseizures**, or psychogenic non-epileptic seizures, mimic epileptic convulsions but lack epileptiform discharges on concurrent electroencephalography. Characteristic features include tightly closed eyes resistant to opening, side-to-side head thrashing, out-of-phase limb movements, pelvic thrusting, preserved pupillary light reflexes, and absence of post-ictal prolactin elevation.
steps.say: Pseudoseizures mimic epilepsy but feature closed eyes resisting opening, pelvic thrusting, intact pupillary reflexes, and normal ictal EEG.

vis.title: Epileptic vs Non-Epileptic Seizures
rows: Open, rolled upward or tonic gaze
Tightly squeezed closed; resists manual opening
Asynchronous thrashing, head shaking, pelvic thrusts
Normal background rhythm with muscle artifact
Stupor, confusion, tongue bite, prolactin rise

steps.tx: **Hoover sign** provides definitive objective neurological validation of functional lower extremity weakness. The examiner places hands beneath both heels while asking the patient to lift the paralyzed leg; in functional weakness, the examiner detects involuntary downward pressure beneath the 'paralyzed' heel when the healthy leg is flexed.
steps.say: Hoover sign tests functional leg paresis: involuntary downward pressure from the weak heel is detected when the patient flexes the opposite healthy leg.

nodes.label: Examiner places both hands beneath the patient's heels in supine position
Instruct patient to elevate the paretic leg (weak downward push detected)
Instruct patient to flex the contralateral healthy leg against resistance
Positive sign: involuntary normal downward push felt beneath the paretic heel

steps.tx: **Somatic symptom disorder** is diagnosed when an individual suffers from one or more distressing physical symptoms, accompanied by disproportionate, persistent thoughts, high anxiety, and excessive time devoted to health concerns. Unlike conversion disorder, the primary diagnostic emphasis is not medical unexplainedness, but the excessive psychological distress.
steps.say: Somatic symptom disorder focuses on excessive anxiety and disproportionate thoughts devoted to physical symptoms, lasting at least six months.

left.title: Somatic Symptom Disorder
points: Distressing somatic pain or gastrointestinal signs
High health-related anxiety and clinic visits

right.title: Conversion Disorder
points: Acute neurological motor or sensory deficits
Evaluated using objective signs like Hoover test
Strong association with acute stress precipitants
